questions.question: India and Canada signed three key agreements on March 2, 2026. Which of the following is NOT one of the sectors covered by these specific MoUs?
questions.solution:

• **Agreements Signed:** Three specific Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were exchanged covering **Critical Minerals**, **Renewable Energy**, and **Cultural Cooperation**.
 
• **Uranium Deal:** A significant 10-year, **$2 billion Uranium supply agreement** was also inked to support India's civil nuclear energy sector.

• **Defence Dialogue:** A new **India-Canada Defence Dialogue** was established to deepen cooperation in maritime security and military exchanges.
 
• **Other Initiatives:** While cooperation in space and quantum tech was discussed and intended (ISRO and CSA), they were part of broader strategic discussions rather than the three primary MoUs signed at this specific ceremony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Context of the Visit__**

• **Sovereign Interests:** For Canada, India represents a critical partner for diversifying trade away from the US; for India, Canada is a key source for **energy security** (Uranium, LNG) and **critical minerals** (Lithium, Cobalt) needed for the green transition.

questions.question: The Big Bang theory was propounded by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**George Lamaitre.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Big Bang Theory** is the most widely accepted theory regarding the origin of the universe.
 
• Big Bang Theory is also called** expanding universe hypothesis.**
 
• The Big Bang theory was propounded by **George Lamaitre.**__
 
• According to Big Bang Theory, the universe originated from a tiny hot body with a giant explosion and it expanded rapidly.
 
• This rapid expansion caused the universe to cool and resulted in its present stage.
 
• Within 300,000 years from the Big Bang, the temperature dropped to 4,500K and gave rise to atomic matter.
 
• The big band occurred approximately **13,75 billion years ago.**
 
• **Edwin Hubble **in 1920 provided evidence that the universe is expanding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Al-Biruni **was the First Muslim Scholar to study Indian tradition.
 
• **Dr. Allen Sundes** is the propounded of "Pulsating Universe Theory".

questions.question: Parkinson’s disease affects which of the following organ in human beings?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The diseases that affect the nervous system & brain are called **neurological disorders**. For example Epilepsy, Alzheimer’s, Meningitis,** Parkinson's disease**, etc.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Parkinson's disease** is a progressive neurological disorder that affects the brain in human beings.
 
• It occurs due to impairment or death of the nerve cells present in the brain that are responsible for the control & coordination of the body.
 
• These nerve cells or neurons produce a neurotransmitter called **dopamine **which is very essential in maintaining the body balance, due to the damage to these neurons the dopamine level falls down.
 
• The symptoms of this disease include tremors or shaking of the hands & legs, difficulty while walking, impairment of the body posture, difficulty in speaking, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act was passed in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was passed to **give the government enormous powers to suppress political activities **by allowing the **detention of political prisoners without trial for two years.** 
 
• It was **recommended **by the **sedition committee chaired by Sir Sidney Rowlatt**. 
 
• It is also known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary crimes act of 1919. **
 
• It invited a large-scale violent **anti-British demonstration** in various places special in Punjab where the situation became explosive. 
 
• **Jallianwala Bagh massacres** were the result of a demonstration against the Rowlatt Act. 
 
• On **9th April 1919, two Nationalist leaders Saifuddin kitchlew and Dr Satyapal **address protest meetings which caused resentment on a large scale. 
 
• On **13th April (Baisakhi) **thousands of **people assembled at the Jallianwala Bagh unaware of the prohibitory orders** which resulted in **open firing against thousands of people on General dyers orders.**

• The new symbol designed by **D Udaya Kumar, a post-graduate of IIT Bombay** was finally selected by the Union Cabinet on 15th July 2010.
 
• Though the symbol will not be printed or embossed on currency notes or coins, it would be included in the **'Unicode standard'.**
 
• The major scripts of the world to ensure that it is easily displaced and printed in the **electronic and print media**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about speed of sound in different media at 25 ºC?

A. In Oxygen gas, the speed of sound is 316 km/s.

B. In water (distilled), the speed of sound is 1498 km/s

options.text: Both A and B is true
Neither A nor B is true

questions.solution:
None of the given statements are true.

__
 
• In Oxygen gas, the speed of sound is **316 m/s** and not **316 km/s.**__
 
• In water (distilled), the speed of sound is around **1498 m/s **and not__ 1498 km/s.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound travels at different speeds depending on what it is traveling through.
 
• Of the three mediums (gas, liquid, and solid) s**ound waves travel the slowest through gases**, faster through liquids, and **fastest through solids.** Temperature also affects the speed of sound.
 
• At freezing (0º Celcius), sound travels through air at 331 meters per second, but, at 20ºC, room temperature, sound travels at 343 meters per second.
 
• Sound travels **faster in liquids** than in gases because **molecules are more tightly packed.**
 
• Sound travels **fastest through solids**. This is because **molecules in a solid medium are much closer together than those in a liquid or gas,** allowing sound waves to travel more quickly through it. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Which dynasty succeeded the Muaryas?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shunga**__.

__
 
• After the Mauryan rule **Pushyamitra**, **the founder of the Shunga dynasty established his rule**__.

 __
 
• The Sungas **ruled** for over a hundred years.
 
• The **extent of the Sunga kingdom under Pushyamitra extended from Punjab and extended to the southern regions of the Narmada**.
 
• The Sunga dynasty had a line of ten rulers.
 
• The **last of the Sunga king was Devabhuti**.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya is the founder** of the Mauryan dynasty.

 
 
• In the wake of the death of **Alexander the Great in 323 BCE, Chandragupta (or Chandragupta Maurya), **conquered the Punjab region from the southeastern edges of Alexander’s former empire.
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty**
 
 
• **Vijayalaya Chola (846-907 AD)**: He was a vassal of the Pallavas. He captured Tanjore from the Pandyas and made it the capital of the Cholas.
 
• **Aditya I (871-907 AD)**: Extended the work of Vijayalaya by occupying the territories from the Pallavas.
 
• **Parantaka Chola I (907-955 AD)**: Was the first imperial Chola.
 
 
• He defeated the Pandyans and Shrilankans initially but was later defeated by the** Rashtrakuta king Krishna III. **
 
 
 
• **Raja Raja Chola I (907-1014 AD)**: Orchestrated the resurgence of the Cholas.
 
 
• Raja Raja, I developed the naval strength of the Cholas
 
• **He re-organized the administrative system**
 
• In 1000 Ad he began the conduction of a land survey
 
• He adopted the practice of inscribing the historical inscriptions
 
• He began the practice of associating Yuvaraja or crown Prince with the administration
 
• Raja Raja I being a patron of Shaivism constructed the great Raja Rajeshwar temple (Also called the Brihadeeswarar temple) at Tanjore.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra I (1014-44 AD)**:
 
 
• He is **considered the greatest Chola ruler**.
 
• He completed the conquest of Sri Lanka in 1017 AD and captured the whole of Sri Lanka and made it a part of the Chola empire. 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Origin of Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire rose to prominence in 320 AD and spread to large parts of northern India, central and small parts of southern India.
 
• **The founder of the Gupta dynasty is Sri Gupta.**
 
• They are thought to be either Brahmins or Vaishyas.

• Those to be implemented by executive orders.
 
 
• Other recommendations to be made by the Finance Commission, as per its Terms of Reference

questions.question: What is the primary function of the NVS-02 satellite launched aboard GSLV-F15?

options.text: It supports meteorological observations for cyclone prediction.
It boosts India's navigation system by offering precise position and timing data.
It conducts deep-space communication with planetary probes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It boosts India's navigation system by offering precise position and timing data.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NVS-02** is part of the NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) satellite system, designed to enhance India's regional navigation capabilities.
 
• The satellite was launched aboard the **GSLV-F15** rocket by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
 
• It primarily strengthens India's indigenous satellite-based navigation system by providing accurate positional and timing data.
 
• The satellite ensures improved accuracy for navigation services across India and a region extending up to 1,500 km beyond Indian borders.
 
• **NVS-02** is equipped with advanced rubidium atomic clocks for precise timekeeping, a critical component for navigation systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India's NavIC System**

 
 
• NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is India's independent regional navigation satellite system developed by ISRO.
 
• It provides accurate position information services to users in India and the surrounding region.
 
• NavIC is comparable to global navigation systems like GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU), and BeiDou (China).
 
• It has applications in terrestrial, aerial, and marine navigation, disaster management, vehicle tracking, and more.

questions.question: Which upcoming wildlife survey in India, scheduled for 2026, is known as the world’s largest and most advanced wildlife census, integrating satellite mapping, AI-driven camera traps, and field tracking to assess tiger populations and ecosystem health?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All India Tiger Estimation (AITE).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• India is preparing for the 2026 All India Tiger Estimation (AITE), the world’s largest and most sophisticated wildlife survey, aimed at assessing tiger populations and overall ecosystem health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) is conducted once every four years and integrates **ground tracking, satellite mapping, and AI-based camera traps** for data collection and analysis.
 
• India, which harbors over **75% of the world’s wild tigers**, recorded 3,682 tigers in the 2022 census.
 
• The 2026 survey will cover over **400,000 sq km** of forest area across 20+ states, involving **more than 60,000 forest staff**.
 
• The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) and the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) are leading the scientific and technological aspects of the survey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Three Phases of AITE 2026**__

 __
 
• **Phase 1 – On-Ground Tracking:** Forest guards patrol 15 km daily, documenting pugmarks, prey sightings, and human activity to assess habitat health.
 
• **Phase 2 – Satellite Integration:** The Wildlife Institute of India uses remote sensing to map forest cover, water sources, and human encroachment for targeted conservation.
 
• **Phase 3 – Camera Traps & AI:** Over 40,000 motion-sensitive cameras will capture tiger images, with AI software identifying individuals through unique stripe patterns.
 
 
 
• **Technological Innovations**__
 __
 
• Combines field data, GIS mapping, and artificial intelligence for precise estimation.
 
• Ensures optimal camera placement through satellite-guided habitat mapping.
 
• Uses advanced analytics to monitor prey density and human-wildlife interfaces.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Impact**__
 __
 
• Helps measure India’s progress toward its **net-zero biodiversity loss goals**.
 
• Guides policies for tiger conservation, habitat restoration, and eco-tourism planning.
 
• Strengthens India’s global leadership in wildlife conservation science.
 
 
 
• **Static Facts**__
 
 
• Survey Name: All India Tiger Estimation (AITE)
 
• Next Census: 2026
 
• Previous Count (2022): 3,682 tigers
 
• Coverage Area: 400,000 sq km
 
• Lead Agency: Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
 
• Collaborating Body: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)

questions.question: Which of the following is the biggest language family of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is an **__Indo-Aryan language__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The **biggest language family **of **India** is the **Indo-Aryan language**.
 
• Indo-Aryan languages, also called **Indic languages**.
 
• It is a subgroup of the Indo-Iranian branch of the Indo-European language family.
 
• Around **74% of Indians speak** a language related to the Indo-Aryan language family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Indo-Aryan languages are generally divided into three major divisions: 
 
 
• Old Indo-Aryan group-** Vedic Sanskrit** was born around this period.

 
 
• Sanskrit is one of the official languages of India and is known as a **classical language** of the country and is also considered to be the **Mother of all Languages**
 
 
 
• Middle Indo-Aryan:- Prakit language was developed during this period.
 
 
• Some languages have originated from Prakrit like Pali, Ardha Magadhi, and Apabharnsha.
 
 
 
• New (Modern) Indo-Aryan:- This group of languages is mainly spoken in northern and western India.
 
 
 
• The Indo-Aryan language family includes mostly all languages of northern and western India such as **Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Sindhi, Rajasthani, Assamese, Oriya, Pahari, Bihari, Kashmiri, Urdu,** and **Sanskrit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mon-Khmer languages**:

 
 
• Mon-Khmer languages have three types **Khmer (Cambodian)**, **Mon **(a minority language in **Myanmar and Thailand**), and **Vietnamese**.
 
 
 
• **North Dravidian language**
 
 
• **​**It is part of the **Dravidian language group**.
 
• In this group languages Brahui(Spoken in Baluchistan), Malto(spoken in tribal areas of Bengal and Odisha), and Kurukh(spoken in Bengal, Odhisha, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh).
 
 
 
• **Telugu** is a Dravidian group language, numerically the **largest of all Dravidian languages**.
 
• **Malayalam** is the **smallest and youngest** of the Dravidian group.

questions.question: Who scored 10 goals for India in their 24-1 victory over the USA to secure a second consecutive Olympic gold medal in hockey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Roop Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Roop Singh was an Indian field hockey player who played a crucial role in India’s historic Olympic victories in the 1930s.
 
• In the 1932 Summer Olympics held in Los Angeles, India defeated the USA with a record-breaking score of 24-1 in hockey.
 
• Roop Singh scored an incredible 10 goals in this match, showcasing his exceptional skill and earning a place in hockey history.
 
• He was the younger brother of Dhyan Chand, often referred to as the “Wizard of Hockey,” and together they formed a legendary duo in Indian hockey.
 
• Roop Singh’s contribution to the game is celebrated as one of the finest performances in Olympic hockey history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhyan Chand:**

 
 
• Dhyan Chand, often referred to as the “Wizard of Hockey,” is widely regarded as one of the greatest hockey players of all time.
 
• He represented India in the Olympics three times (1928, 1932, and 1936) and was instrumental in securing gold medals for the country in all these events.
 
• Dhyan Chand scored multiple goals across these tournaments, earning global fame for his extraordinary dribbling skills and precision.
 
• He received the Padma Bhushan, India’s third-highest civilian award, in 1956 for his contribution to sports.
 
 
 
• **Balbir Singh Sr.:**
 
 
• Balbir Singh Sr. was another legendary hockey player who represented India in the Olympics in later years (1948, 1952, and 1956).
 
• He played a key role in securing three consecutive Olympic gold medals for India.
 
• Balbir Singh Sr. is remembered for scoring five goals in the 1952 Olympic final against the Netherlands, setting a record for the highest number of goals in an Olympic final match.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Shri in recognition of his contributions to Indian hockey.
 
 
 
• **Leslie Claudius:**
 
 
• Leslie Claudius was an Indian hockey player who won three Olympic gold medals (1948, 1952, and 1956) and one silver medal (1960) during his illustrious career.
 
• He was known for his defensive skills and played a key role as a half-back in the Indian hockey team.
 
• Leslie Claudius holds the distinction of being one of the most decorated Olympians in hockey.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Shri for his contributions to the sport of hockey.

questions.question: Name the longest cell in humans.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**Nerve cell**__.

__
 
• Cells are the basic structural and functional unit of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• They are the smallest units of life and hence are also known as the **"building blocks of life"**.
 
• All living organisms are either composed of single cells i.e. unicellular or are multicellular organisms composed of many cells working together.
 
• **Neurons, also **called nerve cells are the **longest cell in humans**.
 
• These are the fundamental units of the brain and nervous system.
 
• **Neurons communicate **with each other as well as with other cells through electric signals which in turn allows effector organs to respond to the stimuli.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is concerned with trade unions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INTUC(Indian National Trade Union Congress)**__.

 
• **INTUC(Indian National Trade Union Congress) **is the Indian National Congress trade union wing.
 
• **Formed on 3 May 1947**, it is affiliated with the International Confederation of Trade Unions.
 
• The founding conference of INTUC was inaugurated by **Acharya JB Kripalani** who was then president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Trade Unions in India are registered under the** Trade Union Act (1926)** and file annual reports accordingly.
 
• Trade Union movement in India is divided mainly along political lines and follows a pattern of contradictory relations between pre-independence political parties and unions.
 
• **Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh** is India's largest trade union.

questions.question: The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is 80°. Then what will be the value of the incident angle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**1**__, i.e. __**40**__°.

According to the **law of reflection** when a ray of light reflects off a surface than the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82f09ac72ab6ae43b5b1150f7458b3e2adb355c1308db63955a77d6a44816541.png] 

 
• Now, **Angle of incidence(i) = Angle of reflection(v)**
 
• According to the question, Angle between the incident ray and reflected ray is 80°.
 
• From the diagram, i + v = 80°
 
• So, 2i = 80°
 
• Then, the** incident angle = 40**°

questions.question: Graphite is a/an?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ****Non-metal.**__

__**Concept**__

__
 
• **Alloy **- Alloys are formed by the combination of two or more metals. Example - Bronze is an alloy of Sn and Cu.
 
• **Metalloid** - Elements that have characteristics of both metals and non-metals.
 
• **Allotrope - **Different crystalline forms of an element. Diamond and **graphite** are allotropes of carbon.

**Explanation**__

__
 
• Carbon is a non-metal therefore its allotrope** graphite is also a non-metal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Non- metal is generally a poor conductor of electricity but some exceptions are there.
 
• Graphite can **conduct electricity **even though it is a non-metal because of the** presence of delocalized electrons in its structure.**

questions.question: A car of mass 800 Kg is moving on an expressway. In order to increase the speed of the car from 54km/hr to 90km/hr the work required to be done will be
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Work-energy theorem: It states that the sum of work done by all the forces acting on a body is equal to the change in the kinetic energy of the body i.e.,

Work done by all the forces = Kf - Ki

W = (1)/(2)m{v²} - (1)/(2)m{u²} = {bf{Δ }}K

Where v = final velocity, u = initial velocity and m = mass of the body

CALCULATION__:

It is given that,
Mass of the car (m) = 800 kg

Final Velocity (v) = 90 km/hr = (90 × 1000)/3600 = 25 m/s

initial velocity (u) = 54 km/hr = (54 × 1000)/3600 = 15 m/s
According to the work-energy theorem,

⇒ Work done = Change in K.E
⇒ W = Δ K.E

⇒ Work done (W) = Final K.E - Initial KE = 1/2 mv2 - 1/2 mu²
⇒ **W = (1/2) × 800 × 252 - (1/2) × 800 × 152 = 250000 - 90000 = 160000 J = 160 kJ**

So option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
The tallest bridge in the world Millau Viaduct has been constructed over the river 

A. Seine

B. Tarn

C. Durance

D. Loire
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Option 2__** i.e __**B**__.

__
 
• **Millau Viaduct**:

 
 
• it is a cable-stayed bridge in France.
 
• It is constructed over the **River Tarn__ **near Millau.
 
• Its designers are the French engineer Michel Virlogeux and British architect Norman Foster.
 
 
 
• **Seine**: 
 
 
• It is a river in France.
 
• The Seine river rises in the Source-Seine.
 
• It flows through Paris and drains into the English Channel at Le Havre.
 
 
 
• **Durance**: 
 
 
• It is a river in France.
 
• It raises in the south-western Alps and flows to the Mediterranean sea.
 
 
 
• **Loire:**
 
 
• It is the largest river in France.
 
• It raises in the Mont Gerbier de Jonc in France.
 
• It flows to the Atlantic Ocean.
